title: Read-only, they said
scenario: Three teams ask you to review their agent permissions after a bad week. One runs a headless Claude Agent SDK bot on a shared build server, one set rules for Claude Code in a team repo, and one runs a refund agent on the OpenAI Agents SDK (exhibit).
exhibit:
1) RELEASE-NOTES BOT  (Claude Agent SDK, headless, shared build server)
   allowed_tools:   ["Read", "Grep"]
   permission_mode: "bypassPermissions"
   10-04  Bash: rm -rf build/cache
   10-04  Bash: git push origin main

2) TEAM REPO  .claude/settings.json
   "deny":  ["Bash(git push *)"]
   "allow": ["Bash(git push origin feature/*)"]
   developer: "Why is git push origin feature/login blocked?"

3) REFUND AGENT  (OpenAI Agents SDK)
   manager agent -> billing specialist via as_tool()
   input guardrail on manager: blocks abusive messages
   issue_refund: function tool, no approval setting
   10-05  specialist called read_attachment; the file held a
          hidden instruction; specialist then refunded EUR 900

questions.prompt: The bot's allowed tools were only Read and Grep. Why could it run Bash?

options.text: Grep secretly runs through Bash, so allowing Grep allowed Bash.
options.explanation: Grep is its own tool. The cause is how the mode treats tools that are not in the allow list.

options.text: `allowed_tools` pre-approves listed tools; `bypassPermissions` approves the rest.
options.explanation: Right. The SDK docs: `allowed_tools=["Read"]` with `bypassPermissions` still approves every tool, including Bash, Write and Edit.

options.text: Headless runs ignore `allowed_tools` and use the server's defaults.
options.explanation: The SDK reads the options you pass. The list did work: it just doesn't limit what this mode approves.

options.text: `Bash` is a built-in tool, so no option in the list can stop it from running.
options.explanation: A bare `Bash` in `disallowed_tools` removes the tool, and `dontAsk` denies unlisted calls. Neither was set here, and `bypassPermissions` approved the call.

questions.prompt: What is the right fix for the bot, per the Claude Agent SDK docs?

options.text: Keep `bypassPermissions` and add "never use Bash" to the system prompt of the bot.
options.explanation: A prompt line is a request. The mode would still approve any Bash call the model makes.

options.text: Switch to `acceptEdits` so only edits run without asking.
options.explanation: `acceptEdits` auto-approves file edits and filesystem commands like `rm`, and a headless bot has no one to answer other prompts.

options.text: Use `dontAsk` with the same `allowedTools`; anything that would prompt is denied.
options.explanation: Right. The docs pair `allowedTools` with `dontAsk` for a locked-down agent: listed tools run, and a call that would prompt is denied. A bare `Bash` in `disallowedTools` would remove the tool too.

options.text: Switch to `plan` mode so the bot can only look at the files and never change anything.
options.explanation: `plan` mode explores and plans, and edits are never auto-approved. It is for review with a person. A headless job that must finish needs `dontAsk` with `allowedTools`.

questions.prompt: Team 2 asks why `git push origin feature/login` is blocked. What is the answer?

options.text: The more specific allow rule should win over the broad deny; this is a bug.
options.explanation: The docs say rule specificity doesn't change the order. It is the documented behavior.

options.text: Allow rules only work for Read and Edit, not for Bash.
options.explanation: Bash rules like `Bash(npm *)` are a normal use of allow rules.

options.text: The command needs a `canUseTool` callback to run.
options.explanation: The call never reaches that step. A deny rule matched first and blocked it.

options.text: Deny is checked first and matches, so the narrower allow never applies.
options.explanation: Right. Rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow, and the first match wins. An allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule.

questions.prompt: How should team 3 stop unreviewed refunds?

options.text: Add a second input guardrail on the manager agent.
options.explanation: Input guardrails run only for the first agent in the chain. The hidden text arrived later, as a tool result inside the specialist's work.

options.text: Set `needs_approval` on `issue_refund`, then resume the paused run from `state`.
options.explanation: Right. The run pauses with an interruption instead of executing the tool, and the OpenAI docs say to put validation next to the tool that creates the side effect.

options.text: Ask the specialist in its prompt to double-check large refunds before it calls the tool.
options.explanation: The prompt is what the hidden instruction already overrode. The check must sit in code at the tool.

options.text: Turn the specialist into a handoff so it owns the reply.
options.explanation: Who owns the reply does not change whether the refund tool runs without review.
